clue.text: Decline drink before round

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it in one
a turn is a round, as in a turn of a wheel

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a drink in favour of buying the next round.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a fall or slump, as in an economic decline.

clue.text: Face briefly people giving stream of abuse

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter of the word for face

parts.note: a dial is a clock face, and slang for a person's face
a tribe is a people or community

explanation.surface: Briefly confronting people who are pouring out insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a torrent of criticism.

clue.text: Lady from western country

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west or western
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A lady who comes from a country in the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a polite synonym for an adult female.

clue.text: Doctor dipping into raised sack? A kind of lottery

indicators.note: dipping into says one piece goes inside another
in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: loot is plunder, what you take when you sack a town
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor reaches into a lifted bag to draw a prize ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a bag for the draw, but it means plunder; 'raised' turns that word into TOOL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle in which tickets are drawn from a revolving drum.

clue.text: Judge speed

definitions.meaning: to assess or rank, a verb
pace, as in the speed at which something moves

explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to assess, and a rate is a pace or velocity.

clue.text: Organised party machine, originally unsystematic

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, so 'organised' gives ran
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word machine

explanation.surface: A political party's well-oiled machine is said to have started out haphazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised party machine' reads as one political phrase, but it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random follows no plan or pattern, i.e. it is haphazard.

clue.text: Opposite an American theatre award on top of mantelpiece

parts.note: the Tony is Broadway's annual theatre award

indicators.note: in a down clue top of picks the first letter of the word mantelpiece

explanation.surface: Facing someone, a Broadway trophy sits on the mantelpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: See dry rot ruined vessel

indicators.note: ruined suggests broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look how dry rot has wrecked the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast warship, a type of naval vessel.

clue.text: One dying for a cause in irregular army crossing centre of Khartoum

indicators.note: crossing says one piece straddles the other, so it goes around it
irregular means not in proper order, so these letters are jumbled
centre of picks the middle two letters of the word Khartoum

explanation.surface: An irregular force crossing central Khartoum is ready to die for its cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges the soldiers' word into MARY, which 'crossing' wraps around the city's middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone killed for their beliefs.

clue.text: The old lady held in reform school

indicators.note: held in says one piece is enclosed by the word for reform

parts.note: to alter something is to change or reform it
'the old lady' is slang for one's mother, mama

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is detained in a reformatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform school' looks like one unit, but 'reform' is the outer piece and 'school' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: One's alma mater is the school or college one attended.

clue.text: Shopkeeper about to make clothes for broadcast

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: for broadcast signals a word as heard on air, not as spelled

parts.note: to tailor is to make clothes

explanation.surface: A store owner about to make outfits for a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer sells goods to the public, as a shopkeeper does.

clue.text: In effect, a serious weapon

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: Said of a weapon that is, in effect, no joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A taser is a stun gun firing electrified darts, a non-lethal weapon.

clue.text: American writer to seek election over there

parts.note: to run is to stand as a candidate in an election
yon is an old word meaning over there

explanation.surface: An American author decides to stand for office abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon was an American short-story writer, author of Guys and Dolls stories.

clue.text: Mean to consume mostly raw fish

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: stingy means mean with money

indicators.note: mostly means drop the final letter of the word for raw

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A miser eats nearly uncooked fish to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' is the outer word here, not the definition; 'mostly' leaves the first two letters of 'raw' to go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat sea creature with a barbed tail, a kind of ray.

clue.text: Forcibly strikes barrier in Kent town

parts.note: rams means hits with force
a gate is a barrier in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Someone smashes into a gate in a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsgate is a seaside port town on the Kent coast.

clue.text: A bit hasty, mate shot nevertheless

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone's mate fired a little too hastily, but so be it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase concedes a point and moves on, meaning however or even so.

clue.text: Difficult assignment given by high command

parts.note: tall means high
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A tough task handed down from top brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high command' reads as the top military leadership, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a request that is hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Working-class twit, silly chap

parts.note: a clot is a fool, like a twit

indicators.note: silly means scatty, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A working man dismissed as a foolish, daft fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat cap is a symbol of labouring men, so the term describes the working class.

clue.text: Group of peers rated rollmops, pickled

indicators.note: pickled suggests something altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords give their verdict on pickled herring.
explanation.walkthrough: Rollmops are pickled herring fillets, so 'pickled' fits the surface while signalling the anagram. The Lords Temporal are the non-bishop members of Britain's House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the secular members of the British upper house, a body of peers.

clue.text: Prize dog not right following run out

indicators.note: following says the trimmed dog comes after the other piece

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: not means leave a letter out of the word for dog

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A prize-winning dog loses out after a run-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' takes R from SETTER to leave SETTE; RO, run out in cricket, comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize, e.g. at a dog show.

clue.text: Satisfied after fruit drop down

indicators.note: after says the first word comes behind the second

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
met means satisfied, as in met a requirement

explanation.surface: Content once the fruit has fallen from the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply.

clue.text: A loud attack may make one scared

parts.note: F is forte, the musical notation for loud
a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: A noisy assault is likely to frighten anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Afraid is a plain synonym for frightened.

clue.text: Paper hat belonging to court jester?

definitions.meaning: a size of writing paper, roughly 13 by 8 inches
read literally, the cap worn by a fool or jester

explanation.surface: Asking whether the paper hat belongs to the court jester.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a paper size named after a jester's-cap watermark, and literally a fool's cap.

clue.text: Boy in abbreviated game, forward

parts.note: RU is the short form of rugby union
forward can mean cheeky or impudent, i.e. pert

explanation.surface: A lad plays in a shortened match in the forward position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests a rugby position, but here it means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is a male first name, so it stands for a boy.

clue.text: Section of text? Rather more

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asked whether a section is part of a text, the reply is that it's an addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, over and above, i.e. further.

clue.text: Cover old open-air pool

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: An old outdoor pool is covered over.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public outdoor swimming pool.

clue.text: Examination of accounts of car manufacturer close to Detroit

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word Detroit

explanation.surface: A car firm has its books inspected near America's motor city.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is a formal inspection of a firm's financial records.

clue.text: Obscure opening in chess game — it, I suspect must involve knight

indicators.note: must involve says the word for knight is taken inside the other letters
suspect means dubious, so the letters are mixed up
opening in points to the first letter of the word chess

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A chess game's opening is murky; a knight must be involved, the speaker suspects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges the pool into EIGMATIC; 'must involve' then takes the knight in after the E. 'Obscure' looks like it describes the opening, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means puzzling or mysterious, hard to understand.

clue.text: County's staff returned, ready

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: returned means the word for staff is written backwards

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: A county's staff have come back and are prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' reads as employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county on England's south coast.

clue.text: Affected by kick in correctional facility

indicators.note: by says one word is placed next to the other, here after it

parts.note: to boot is to kick
camp means affected or theatrical in manner

explanation.surface: Someone is moved by a kick received inside a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot camp is a strict training or detention centre for young offenders.
